penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: NTFRS-to-DFSR migration must be executed in the customer's specific AD environment — scripted guidance alone is not deliverable; an engineer must run the steps against real domain controllers, validate replication health, and handle failures. Each engagement is per-customer manual work.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: MSP onboarding engagements involve scoping calls, environment assessment, and go/no-go decisions that require live interaction with the client's sysadmin.

rationale: The buyer is identifiable and reachable — MSP owners and sysadmins who bill onboarding hours are a real, nameable segment active on r/msp and Spiceworks — but the service cannot run hands-off. Every migration touches a unique live Active Directory environment; Claude can generate a step-by-step runbook but cannot execute PowerShell against a customer's domain controllers, validate DFSR replication convergence, or recover from journal-wrap errors without a human engineer on-site or in a remote session. Operational autonomy (4) and buildability (5) both fall below build gates, and the penalties for per-customer fulfillment and synchronous engagement drop the total to 2.2, well below even the validate floor.
solution_plan: No viable hands-off plan exists for a solo non-technical operator. The deliverable — safely migrating a production Active Directory environment from NTFRS to DFSR — requires executing privileged commands against live infrastructure, monitoring replication, and responding to failures in real time. Claude can produce a high-quality runbook or checklist (a one-time document product), but that is a commodity that MSPs can find for free on Microsoft Docs. A paid, managed migration service would require a Windows Server engineer as the actual fulfillment layer, making this a staffing/consulting business, not a factory-compatible micro-service Youval can run alone.
notes: Failing build gates: operational_autonomy (4 < 7 required), buildability_with_ai (5 < 6 required). Post-penalty total of 2.2 is well below the 5.5 validate threshold. Drop. A potential adjacent idea worth a separate signal: a self-serve AD health-check report (read-only, no execution) could be more automatable — but that is a different opportunity.
